item.title: Europe Seeks a Lasting UN Security Council Role on AI
item.description: As rotating president of the Security Council in October, Greece is planning to draw attention to a topic close to Athens’ heart: Artificial intelligence and maritime security. Latvia, which holds the Council presidency of the 15-member body in November, is also expected to highlight artificial intelligence in a broad thematic discussion on emerging technologies. item.title: UN aid operation underway in Nepal following fresh floods
item.description: The United Nations has rushed to assist Nepal following new flash floods in the central Gorkha district on Sunday that swept away homes and bridges just weeks after catastrophic flooding in the north.

item.title: ‘Efficiency has limits’: UNHCR chief warns refugee protection is buckling under cuts
item.description: The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year – and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.

item.title: Rise in poverty is ‘a wake-up call for the world’, UN development chief says
item.description: The number of people living in “multidimensional” poverty has risen for the first time in 15 years, reaching 1.2 billion, as families struggle to meet their basic needs.

item.title: General Assembly adopts pandemic declaration, but not by consensus
item.description: The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, by 153 in favour to three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) with two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).

item.title: Colombia peace deal must endure as insecurity grows, Security Council hears
item.description: Nearly 10 years after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement to end a decades-long insurgency, the deal is under strain from growing insecurity – and the UN’s top official in the country says it cannot be allowed to falter.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s fragile transition – economic strain, Israeli incursions and progress towards elections
item.description: The Security Council is meeting on Syria as the country’s transition faces pressure on several fronts. Economic hardship is fuelling unrest, Israeli incursions continue in the south and sectarian tensions persist in Sweida, even as Damascus reports progress on its chemical weapons programme and talks about future elections. Millions, meanwhile, remain displaced. Follow live below and go here for full meetings coverage.

item.title: Sudan: Drought and war push Darfur and Kordofan towards famine
item.description: The risk of famine is growing in parts of Sudan already torn apart by war, as a severe El Niño drought makes life even harder in Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, the UN-backed global hunger monitor warned on Monday.

item.title: How Nepal is Learning To Cope With the Psychological Toll of Its Missing

item.title: Kazakhstan Has Spent 23 Years Bringing Faiths Together. Now Comes the Harder Part.
item.description: Religious leaders and international officials meeting in Astana say a forum built to bridge differences must show that dialogue can produce meaningful action.
